title: Creating with David Choe: Live Art Tutorial
summary: A 4:11 two-person live-art improvisation whose useful shape differs from the broad tutorial title. A damaged performative opening gives way to a question about being done messing around; the primary performer says he will never stop because messing around is his living. A brush plan collapses when he discovers stuff under the stuff. He repeatedly asks about feeling used, abused, discarded like trash or dead inside, says that is how he feels now, then turns a found dead leaf into a parable: perhaps it was leaf or fruit living with sibling leaves on a beautiful tree/Nirvana, expecting permanence until life changed. Fruits/starfruit are repaired; durian, papayas and mangoes remain imagined possibilities. The close searches for black material, incorporates being unprepared and asks about caps. Every repetition and emotional idea remains. Long sound/visual/action spans and the 0.01-second duplicate are explicit; the opening performance, unknown this sound/action, sensory/material transition, cap type and both voices remain unresolved. The archive does not invent a guest, diagnosis, current self-harm crisis, therapy advice or complete technical tutorial.
